sources.title: Install and run the neural text to speech container
sources.what_it_established: Tag format is <version>-amd64-<locale>-<voicename>; :latest pulls en-US/en-us-arianeural; the locale of the SSML voice must correspond to the locale of the container model

welsh.evidence: Language-support table rows: `| `cy-GB` | Welsh (United Kingdom) | Standard | `cy-GB-NiaNeural`<sup>3</sup> (Female) |` and `cy-GB-AledNeural`<sup>3</sup> (Male). Both carry footnote 3: "Phonemes, custom lexicon, and visemes aren't supported."
welsh.rationale: Welsh is a first-class listed locale with a male and a female neural voice, and it is what cym_n_for_eng and cym_s_for_eng already run on. The caveat is real and belongs in the report: on Welsh specifically Azure gives you NO phoneme override and NO custom lexicon, so a mispronounced Welsh word cannot be corrected by markup — only by respelling the input text. Welsh is also not offered as an HD/Dragon locale, so the temperature control does not exist there either.

version_pinning: NONE for the classic neural voices we use. Microsoft Q&A 2026-02-11: "Azure Speech does not provide version pinning for standard neural or multilingual voices" and "Once the backend model is replaced, the older version is retired and becomes inaccessible", with no guaranteed advance notice. HD voices name a base model and version (voicename:basemodel:version) but every documented voice id is the ...LatestNeural form, which the docs define as "Always uses the latest version of the DragonHD base model". The only genuine pin available anywhere in the Azure line is the neural-text-to-speech CONTAINER image, which you host and therefore choose when to upgrade. Product-level deprecation policy is real and generous: standard (non-neural) voices were announced 2021-08-31 and retired 2024-08-31 — about three years of notice — but that policy governs the PRODUCT tier, not the model weights behind a named voice.
cloning_consent: Custom Neural Voice is Limited Access: eligibility review via an intake form (aka.ms/customneural). A recording of the voice talent reading a consent statement must be submitted before fine-tuning. Responsible-AI disclosure guidance and a code of conduct apply. Personal Voice is a separate, lighter product with its own consent gate.

controls.seed: None. No seed parameter exists on any Azure TTS surface.
controls.temperature: Not available on the classic neural voices we use. Available on HD voices only, via SSML parameters="temperature=0.8" — DragonHD default 1.0, Dragon HD Omni default 0.7 with top_p (0.7), top_k (22) and cfg_scale (1.4). Welsh has no HD voice, so this control is unreachable for Welsh.
controls.other: Full SSML on classic neural voices: <prosody rate/pitch/volume>, <break>, <phoneme> (ipa/sapi/ups/x-sampa), <lexicon> pointing at an uploaded PLS file (100 KB max), <say-as>, <sub>, <lang>, <mstts:express-as> styles, viseme and word-boundary events. HD voices support only a subset (no <prosody>, no <emphasis>, no <break> on Omni). Footnote 3 locales — Welsh among them — lose <phoneme>, <lexicon> and visemes entirely.

self_host: YES, but it does not reach Welsh. mcr.microsoft.com/azure-cognitive-services/speechservices/neural-text-to-speech runs on-prem (6 core / 12 GB minimum, 8 core / 16 GB recommended), and a disconnected variant runs with no internet on application approval plus a commitment plan. The image is ONE LOCALE AND ONE VOICE PER TAG (3.11.0-amd64-en-us-arianeural; :latest is en-US/AriaNeural). A pinned container digest is the only way to freeze an Azure voice against a backend model swap. VERIFIED 2026-08-26 against the public MCR tag list (https://mcr.microsoft.com/v2/azure-cognitive-services/speechservices/neural-text-to-speech/tags/list, 5,458 tags): 60 locales are published and cy-GB IS NOT ONE OF THEM. The container covers 30 of our 68 target languages; 21 Azure cloud languages have no image at all (afr bul cat cym ell est eus gle glg hrv hun hye isl lav lit mkd mlt nep ron srp swa). So the strongest repeatability mechanism on the board misses the gate-zero language and over half the estate.
pricing: $15.00 per 1M characters (S1 Neural Text To Speech Characters, Azure Retail Prices API, USD). Free tier 0.5M characters/month. Commitment tiers cut it to roughly $5.70-$12.00 per 1M. Custom Neural Voice synthesis $24/1M realtime, HD $48/1M, plus $52/compute-hour training and $4.032/hour model hosting.
rate_limits: Real-time TTS: F0 20 transactions per 60 seconds (not adjustable). S0 30 transactions per second default, adjustable on request up to 1,000 TPS. Batch synthesis: no limit on concurrent active jobs. 429 on burst; Microsoft documents a 1-2-4-4 minute back-off ramp.

files: services/azure-tts-service.cjs:157-171 (buildSSML, locale derived from the voice name)
live_integration.endpoint: Two paths. (1) The microsoft-cognitiveservices-speech-sdk via SpeechConfig.fromSubscription(key, region) — services/tts-service.cjs:329 and services/azure-tts-service.cjs:128. (2) A raw REST path at https://<region>.tts.speech.microsoft.com/cognitiveservices/v1 with Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key and Content-Type: application/ssml+xml — tools/a108/a131-blind-raw-tts.cjs:78.
live_integration.settings_we_send: voiceName passed VERBATIM from voice_config.voiceId (Azure "xx-XX-NameNeural" form) at services/voice-config-service.cjs:461 — an "azure_" storage prefix is stripped only in the VoiceLab list builder (services/voicelab/params.cjs:99), never on the render path. Region from AZURE_SPEECH_REGION defaulting to westeurope (services/voice-config-service.cjs:460). Output format Audio16Khz32KBitRateMonoMp3 on the tts-service path (services/tts-service.cjs:330) but Audio24Khz96KBitRateMonoMp3 on the azure-tts-service path (services/azure-tts-service.cjs:129) — two different bitrates for the same estate. SSML carries exactly one control: <prosody rate="+N%"> from the cadence speed. We attach a wordBoundary handler and persist the boundaries (services/tts-service.cjs:336-343). We send NO temperature, NO style, NO <phoneme>, NO <lexicon>.
live_integration.determinism_notes: The repo asserts Azure determinism in a comment — "Azure TTS is deterministic - same text = same audio" (services/azure-tts-service.cjs:174-178) — and BUILDS ON IT: REGENERATION_VARIATIONS mutates the punctuation of the input text (append ".", append "...", insert a comma before the last word) purely to force different audio out of a voice that will otherwise return the same bytes. That is a working determinism test in production, not a doc claim. Two things it does not cover: (a) it says nothing about determinism ACROSS TIME, which is exactly where Azure has changed models under customers; (b) it is untrue of HD voices, which the docs say vary per output — we do not currently use any HD voice, and nothing in the code stops one being configured. The SSML envelope in services/tts-service.cjs:353 hardcodes xml:lang="en-US" while azure-tts-service.cjs:163 derives the locale from the voice name; the voice element overrides it in practice, but the two paths are not the same request.

gaps: CLOSED 2026-08-26: the neural-text-to-speech container does NOT ship cy-GB. The public MCR tag list has 60 locales and Welsh is absent, so Welsh cannot be frozen on-prem and Welsh repeatability rests on the human recordings, not on any pinning mechanism. Still unverified: whether Microsoft would build a cy-GB image on enterprise request - a sales question, not a docs question.

The public azure.microsoft.com pricing page rendered placeholder dashes on fetch; the figures here come from the Azure Retail Prices API instead. The API returned two S1 Neural TTS rows ($15.00 and $18.75 per 1M) which are presumably different regional meters — the region attribution was not resolved.

No Microsoft document states a formal deprecation or notice policy for INDIVIDUAL neural voices. The three-year standard-voice retirement is a product-tier policy. The only statement found about individual voice model swaps is a Microsoft Q&A answer, which is a support channel, not a published SLA.
Whether Azure classic neural voices are byte-identical across regions, or across SDK versions, is not documented and was not tested (phase 1 spends zero).
Serbian appears as both sr-RS (Cyrillic) and sr-LATN-RS (Latin); which our srp courses need was not checked.

nan (Min Nan) is marked yes on the strength of footnote 6 only — nan-CN is a SECONDARY locale of the single voice zh-CN-XiaoxiaoDialectsNeural, not a first-class locale with its own voices. Treat that yes as weaker than the others.
